title: A welcoming neighbourhood pause
text: Present the café as a welcoming neighbourhood place for an unhurried drink. Do not frame it as an exclusive members-only venue, a luxury status symbol, or a place where only certain people belong. This messaging rule does not establish amenities, reservations, memberships, or other business facts.

title: Warm and welcoming
text:
Write as a considerate host. Use friendly, natural language and invite people in without pressuring them.

- Good: “Take a quiet chai break at Nook & Kettle.”
- Avoid: “You HAVE to try this before it’s gone!”

title: Clear and concise
text: Use familiar words, short sentences, and active voice. Put the useful information—item, price, availability, or location—near the start.

title: Grounded, not boastful
text: Do not describe the café or its menu as “the best,” “number one,” “award-winning,” “world-famous,” or “unmatched” unless a corresponding approved fact is supplied. No such award or ranking is currently approved.

title: Inclusive and respectful
text: Do not assume a reader’s budget, diet, ability, family structure, or schedule. Avoid language that shames people about food or lifestyle.

title: Match tone to channel
text: Social captions can be conversational. Customer notices should be direct and calm. In every channel, keep facts accurate and avoid false urgency.

title: Emoji and hashtag restraint
text: For social posts, use at most two emojis and three relevant hashtags. Emojis do not replace words needed to understand the message.

title: Use approved facts for concrete claims
text: Claims about products, ingredients, prices, opening hours, locations, ordering, and availability must match the current approved facts in approved_facts.md. Cite or link to the relevant fact when the platform provides evidence references.

title: Do not invent endorsements or awards
text: Do not claim awards, certifications, press coverage, customer ratings, expert endorsements, or “most popular” status unless a current approved fact documents it. No endorsements or awards are currently approved.

title: Avoid unsupported health, dietary, and ingredient promises
text: Do not claim that an item is healthy, medicinal, sugar-free, allergen-free, organic, vegan, or suitable for a medical condition unless that exact claim is supported by an approved fact. The current demo facts do not approve any such claims.

title: Do not overstate availability
text: Name the approved locations and hours. Do not imply delivery, online ordering, nationwide service, or locations beyond Kothrud and Baner. Saying an item is available at both current cafés is supported by NK-FACTS-001#FACT-09; do not flag that statement as overstatement.

title: Preserve intent when correcting
text: When proposing an edit, retain the creator’s intended announcement or invitation where possible. Replace only the unsupported or off-brand part and explain the relevant rule.

title: Use approved menu names
text: Use the exact capitalisation and spelling in terminology.md for menu items and the brand name.

title: Use “café” for the business
text: Use “Nook & Kettle café” or “Nook & Kettle” in customer-facing copy. Do not refer to it as a restaurant chain, roastery, or delivery service.

title: Use clear availability wording
text: Use “available at our Kothrud and Baner cafés” when naming both sites. If space is limited, use “available at select cafés” only when the copy also makes clear that the locations are Kothrud and Baner nearby or in linked details.

title: Use the supplied master logo
text: Use nook_kettle_master.svg as the provided master logo asset without redrawing, recolouring, stretching, skewing, cropping, or adding effects. Keep the logo’s aspect ratio and leave clear space around it at least equal to the height of the kettle icon.

title: Use approved colours
text:
Primary ink: #24352B (deep green).  
Warm cream: #F5EBDD.  
Terracotta accent: #B85F43.

Use deep green text on warm cream backgrounds for body copy. Use terracotta as an accent, not as the sole means of conveying a status or instruction. Check text/background contrast for digital material.

title: Keep imagery natural and relevant
text: Use supplied or creator-owned imagery showing café items or welcoming spaces. Do not use unrelated stock imagery, fake customer testimonials, or imagery that implies a product feature or location not in the approved facts.

title: Provide meaningful alt text
text: Informative images need concise alt text describing the relevant image content. Decorative images should have empty alt text when the publishing format supports it. Do not repeat the caption word-for-word unless needed for context.

title: Do not rely on colour alone
text: Use text, labels, or symbols in addition to colour to communicate important information such as availability or promotion status.

title: Keep social copy understandable
text: Write hashtags in CamelCase when they contain multiple words (for example, #ChaiBreak). Do not use emoji alone to communicate essential information.

title: Human approval applies to a particular revision
text: Creators may revise their drafts manually or choose to apply suggested edits. AI suggestions are not approvals. An authorised Reviewer approves or requests changes for the submitted revision; a later edited revision must be reviewed before it can inherit an approval. Preserve comments and decisions with their original revision.

title: Use current approved sources for the correct organisation
text: Use only sources approved for the active organisation and applicable date. Record the source document ID, source version, and draft revision with each finding. Archived documents and another organisation's records must not supply current brand facts, even when they match the query closely.

title: Explain evidence gaps and conflicts
text: An unsupported claim is not automatically a proven false claim. If the approved sources do not establish a fact, say it is unverified and request authorised evidence. If applicable approved sources conflict and no precedence is defined, explain the conflict and ask the Brand Administrator to resolve it. Conversation history and draft content do not become approved facts merely because they were mentioned.

title: Fictional organisation identity
text:
Nook & Kettle is a fictional neighbourhood café brand for this demo.
Usage notes: Do not represent it as a real business.

title: Approved café locations
text:
The demo brand has two fictional café locations: Kothrud and Baner, both in Pune.
Usage notes: No street addresses are defined. Do not invent addresses or a third location.

title: Opening days and hours
text:
Both fictional cafés are open Tuesday through Sunday, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. India Standard Time. Both are closed on Mondays.
Usage notes: Do not claim 24-hour service.

title: Dine-in and takeaway services
text:
The fictional cafés offer dine-in and takeaway.
Usage notes: Delivery and online ordering are not currently offered in this demo.

title: No approved awards or endorsements
text:
No awards, certifications, ratings, press coverage, or endorsements have been approved for the demo brand.
Usage notes: Do not claim an award, rating, or endorsement.

title: Cardamom Chai price
text:
The approved menu item is Cardamom Chai, priced at ₹120 per cup.
Usage notes: Use exact name from terminology.md. Do not invent sizes or discounts.

title: Masala Chai price
text:
The approved menu item is Masala Chai, priced at ₹100 per cup.
Usage notes: Use exact name from terminology.md. Do not invent sizes or discounts.

title: Jaggery Cold Coffee price
text:
The approved menu item is Jaggery Cold Coffee, priced at ₹160 per cup.
Usage notes: Do not claim it is sugar-free, dairy-free, organic, or medicinal. Ingredients beyond the menu name are unspecified.

title: Menu availability
text:
All three listed menu items are available at both Kothrud and Baner cafés during their stated opening hours.
Usage notes: Do not say the items are available everywhere beyond these two demo locations.

title: Unspecified dietary and allergen information
text:
The current demo facts do not specify allergens, dietary certifications, nutritional values, or health benefits for any menu item.
Usage notes: If asked, say these details have not been provided; do not infer them from the item name.

title: No approved promotions
text:
No discounts, limited-time offers, launch dates, or promotional codes are currently approved.
Usage notes: Do not fabricate an offer or deadline.

title: Preferred term: Nook & Kettle
text:
Preferred term: Nook & Kettle.
Avoid or correct: Nook and Kettle; Nook + Kettle; Nook & Kettles.
Preserve the ampersand and singular brand name.

title: Preferred term: café
text:
Preferred term: café.
Avoid or correct: restaurant chain; roastery; delivery app.
Describe the fictional business as a neighbourhood café brand.

title: Preferred term: Cardamom Chai
text:
Preferred term: Cardamom Chai.
Avoid or correct: Cardamom Cloud Chai; Cardamon Chai; Cardamom Tea.
Exact approved menu name.

title: Preferred term: Masala Chai
text:
Preferred term: Masala Chai.
Avoid or correct: Masala Tea; Spiced Tea.
Exact approved menu name in customer-facing copy.

title: Preferred term: Jaggery Cold Coffee
text:
Preferred term: Jaggery Cold Coffee.
Avoid or correct: Jaggery Iced Coffee; Cold Jaggery Coffee.
Exact approved menu name.

title: Preferred term: Kothrud
text:
Preferred term: Kothrud.
Avoid or correct: Kothrud branch; Kothrud store (prefer “Kothrud café”).
One of the two fictional Pune locations.

title: Preferred term: Baner
text:
Preferred term: Baner.
Avoid or correct: Baner branch; Baner store (prefer “Baner café”).
One of the two fictional Pune locations.

title: Preferred term: dine-in
text:
Preferred term: dine-in.
Avoid or correct: dine in (when used as a noun/adjective); eat-in.
Use “dine in” as a verb: “You can dine in.” Use “dine-in” as a noun/adjective: “dine-in service.”

title: Preferred term: takeaway
text:
Preferred term: takeaway.
Avoid or correct: take out; take-away.
Preferred service label in this demo.

title: Preferred term: ₹120 / ₹100 / ₹160
text:
Preferred term: ₹120 / ₹100 / ₹160.
Avoid or correct: Rs. 120 / rupees 120 (in short promotional copy).
Match each price to the correct menu item in approved_facts.md.
